title: UK Graduate Route Visa 2026
excerpt: UK Graduate visa length changes in 2027. Apply on or before Dec. 31, 2026 to keep 2 years of post-study stay; from Jan. 1, 2027 it is 18 months. Free guidance by Admizz Education.

content.html:
Every year, thousands of Nepali students choose the UK for higher education — and the Graduate Route visa is one of the biggest reasons why. But in 2026, the rules are changing in ways that directly affect your plans. This guide breaks down exactly what is happening, what it means for students from Nepal, and what you need to do right now to protect your future.

Quick Facts at a Glance

What Is the UK Graduate Route Visa?

The UK Graduate Route — widely known as the Post-Study Work (PSW) visa — is a visa that lets you stay and work in the UK after successfully completing an eligible degree from a UK university. It was reintroduced in 2021 and has since become one of the strongest selling points of studying in the UK for Nepali students.

Unlike most UK work visas, you do not need a job offer, employer sponsorship, or a minimum salary to apply. In other words, you can graduate, apply for this visa, and then take your time finding the right job — all while legally living and working in the UK. You can work in any sector, switch employers freely, freelance, or even start your own business during this period.

For Nepali graduates, this has been a life-changing opportunity — the chance to earn in pounds, gain international experience, and build a long-term career abroad. However, the rules are tightening, and the window to act is getting smaller. Understanding what is changing in 2026 is therefore more important than ever.

🇳🇵 Why this matters for Nepali students specifically: Nepal is consistently among the top source countries for UK student visas. With the new changes, students who do not plan their course completion and visa timing carefully could lose six months of valuable post-study work time — or miss the two-year window entirely.

The 3 Major Changes Nepali Students Must Know in 2026

1. Post-Study Stay Is Being Reduced from 2 Years to 18 Months

This is the most significant update. The UK Home Office has confirmed that from January 1, 2027, the Graduate Route visa will be cut from two years to 18 months for Bachelor's and Master's graduates. That is six fewer months to find a sponsored job, build professional networks, and secure your long-term immigration status in the UK.

However, there is a critical window of opportunity. If you apply on or before December 31, 2026, you will still receive the full two years. If you apply on or after January 1, 2027, the visa lasts 18 months. PhD and doctoral graduates remain unaffected and will continue to receive three years.

⚠️ Key reminder: GOV.UK says the two-year period depends on when you apply: on or before December 31, 2026. Processing usually takes up to 8 weeks, but the decision date does not change the length. Nepali students finishing their degrees in late 2026 should apply as soon as their university notifies the Home Office, so the application is in before the deadline.

2. The Application Fee Is £937 (Approximately NPR 1,58,000)

GOV.UK lists the Graduate visa application fee as £937. This is in addition to the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS), which is paid separately. For Nepali students managing tight budgets, factoring this cost into your financial planning early — ideally before arriving in the UK — is strongly advised.

3. English Language Requirements for the Student Visa

To get your Student visa, GOV.UK requires English at CEFR Level B2 (or equivalent) for degree-level study and B1 below degree level, and your university may assess this itself. For Nepali students, this means your IELTS or other approved test scores need to reflect this standard. If you completed a degree taught in English at a UK university, this is typically considered satisfied — but confirm this with your institution before applying.

Who Can Apply? Eligibility for Nepali Students

To qualify for the Graduate Route as a Nepali student, all of the following must be true at the time of your application:

  • You completed a UK bachelor's, postgraduate, or other eligible course at a Home Office-approved university
  • You held a valid UK Student visa (or Tier 4) during your studies
  • Your university has officially notified the Home Office that you completed your course
  • You are physically present inside the UK when you apply
  • You apply before your Student visa expires — do not overstay
  • You have not previously been granted a Graduate Route or Doctorate Extension Scheme visa
  • You studied in person in the UK — online or distance learning students are not eligible

Additionally, if your education was funded by a government or international scholarship that covered both tuition fees and living costs, you will need written consent from your sponsor. Students funded by universities, private companies, or independent schools do not need this consent.

🇳🇵 Note for Nepali government scholarship holders: If you received a Government of Nepal scholarship or a bilateral scholarship covering your full costs, check with your scholarship body about consent requirements before applying for the Graduate Route.

Important Dates and Deadlines for 2026

May – October 2026
Peak UK graduation season. Most universities notify the Home Office during this period. Apply as soon as you get confirmation — every week of delay matters.
December 31, 2026
Last day to receive the 2-year Graduate Route visa. Your application must be submitted on or before this date to qualify for 2 years. A decision usually takes up to 8 weeks.
January 1, 2027
18-month rule takes effect. All Graduate Route applications from this date lead to only 18 months for Bachelor's and Master's graduates.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide for Nepali Students

The entire Graduate Route application is done online and must be submitted while you are physically in the UK. Here is the process from start to finish:

1
Check your university has notified the Home Office Contact your university's international student office and confirm they have reported your successful completion to the Home Office. You do not need to wait for your graduation ceremony or certificate.
2
Gather your documents You will need your Nepali passport, your Biometric Residence Permit (BRP), and your original CAS number from your Student visa application. If you had a government scholarship, you may also need written sponsor consent.
3
Apply online through GOV.UK only Complete the application at the official UK Government website. Pay the fee (£937) and the Immigration Health Surcharge. Never use unofficial or third-party websites.
4
Complete your identity verification Use the UKVI app for a digital ID check or attend an in-person biometric appointment. The digital route is faster and is recommended where possible.
5
Wait for your decision — up to 8 weeks You can remain in the UK and continue working under your Student visa conditions while your Graduate Route application is being processed.
6
Start planning your next step immediately Once approved, begin networking, applying for graduate jobs, and researching the Skilled Worker visa — so you are not under pressure when the Graduate Route nears its end.

What Comes After the Graduate Route?

The Graduate Route cannot be extended and does not directly lead to settlement. That is why planning your next visa step from day one is essential — not something to leave until the final few months.

Skilled Worker Visa — The Most Common Next Step

Most Nepali graduates on the Graduate Route transition to the Skilled Worker visa after securing employment. To qualify, you need a job offer from a UK employer with a Home Office sponsor licence, a role at RQF Level 3 or above, and a salary of at least £41,700 or the going rate for the occupation, whichever is higher. Time spent on this visa counts toward Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) — the pathway to long-term settlement in the UK.

Starting a Business

The Graduate Route permits self-employment, so you can legally launch a freelance career or start a company during your stay. Many Nepali graduates use this time to build an income stream or test a business idea before transitioning to the Innovator Founder visa.

Pursuing a PhD

If you continue to a doctoral program, you can switch to a Student visa and later access the three-year Graduate Route — giving you significantly more time to establish your career in the UK. For Nepali students who are academically inclined, this remains one of the strongest long-term strategies.

Strategic Tips for Nepali Students Planning to Study in the UK

  • Choose your UK university and course carefully — not all institutions are equal for visa sponsorship and graduate employment outcomes
  • Begin your job search and professional networking from Year 1, not your final semester
  • Target employers and graduate schemes that actively recruit international students and hold sponsor licences
  • Use internships, placement years, and part-time work to build relationships with potential future employers
  • Research the £41,700 Skilled Worker salary threshold and select a career field that realistically meets it
  • If research interests you, strongly consider a PhD — doctoral graduates still receive three years of post-study stay
  • Confirm your university's completion notification timeline early to avoid application delays
  • Work with a registered education consultant in Nepal to plan your UK application, visa timing, and career pathway from the start

Why Nepali Students Still Choose the UK in 2026

Despite the changes to the Graduate Route, the UK remains one of the most popular study destinations for Nepali students — and for very good reasons. To begin with, UK degrees are globally recognized and can be completed in a shorter timeframe than equivalent programs in many other countries. A Bachelor's degree typically takes three years, and a Master's just one year, which means lower total costs and a faster entry into the job market.

Furthermore, the Graduate Route — even at 18 months — still provides more flexibility than many other countries' post-study work arrangements. There is no job offer requirement, no salary minimum, and no restriction on the type of work. For Nepali graduates who are proactive about their job search, 18 months is sufficient time to secure sponsored employment and transition to the Skilled Worker route.

Finally, the UK has a large, established Nepali community, which makes settling in considerably easier for many students. From places of worship and community organizations to Nepali restaurants and events, the support network available to Nepali students in cities like London, Manchester, and Leeds is genuinely strong.

Frequently Asked Questions from Nepali Students

Can Nepali students apply for the Graduate Route visa? +
Yes. The Graduate Route is open to all nationalities, including Nepali students, provided you completed an eligible degree at a Home Office-approved UK university while holding a valid Student visa and you are applying from inside the UK.
Do I need a job offer to apply for the Graduate Route? +
No. This is one of the biggest advantages of the Graduate Route for Nepali graduates. You do not need a job offer, employer sponsorship, or a minimum salary to apply. You can work in any role while searching for the right opportunity.
What is the Graduate Route fee in Nepali Rupees? +
The fee is £937 on GOV.UK. Based on current exchange rates, this is approximately NPR 1,55,000–1,62,000, though you should check the latest rate at the time of your application. The Immigration Health Surcharge is paid separately.
I am finishing my Master's in late 2026. Will I get 2 years or 18 months? +
It depends on when you apply. If you apply on or before December 31, 2026, you receive two years; from January 1, 2027 it is 18 months. Apply as soon as your university notifies the Home Office of your completion, so the application is in well before the deadline.
Can I bring my family to the UK on the Graduate Route? +
Your partner and children can apply to remain in the UK on the Graduate Route — but only if they are already in the UK as dependants on your Student visa. New dependants cannot join you once you are on the Graduate Route. Make sure your family members apply before your Student visa expires.
Can I extend my Graduate Route visa? +
No. The Graduate Route cannot be extended under any circumstances. Once it expires, you must switch to another visa — typically the Skilled Worker visa — or leave the UK. This is why planning your career transition from the very beginning of your post-study stay is so important.
Does the Graduate Route lead to permanent residence (ILR)? +
Not directly. However, it is a strong stepping stone to the Skilled Worker visa, which does count toward the qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR). Most Nepali graduates who settle long-term in the UK follow the path: Graduate Route → Skilled Worker → ILR.
What IELTS score do I need to study in the UK as a Nepali student? +
Requirements vary by university and course level, but most UK universities require an IELTS Academic score of 6.0–6.5 overall for undergraduate programs and 6.5–7.0 for postgraduate. For a UK Student visa, GOV.UK requires CEFR B2 or equivalent at degree level. Always check the specific requirements of your chosen university and course.
